buyer_reported_costs.finding: Among 30 agencies that publish a monthly fee and no one-time price, the median retainer is $5,000/mo, ranging $2,000-$15,000/mo; among 140 agencies publishing a one-time entry price, the median is $2,000 (range $47 to $300,000) and 99 of 140 start below $5,000.
buyer_reported_costs.context: Third-party statistical report over 290 indexed agencies, 205 of which publish prices; these are published list prices, not invoices. Published entry prices only - the same report shows 113 of 205 publishers sit in the $1k-$5k minimum-budget tier.

The profile URL returns HTTP 403, so these two fields come from the listing as surfaced in search results, not from the page body. The same listing's 'most common project size' figure (previously reported here as $10,000-$49,999 from 5 of 8 reviews) could not be confirmed and has been removed.

what_is_included_vs_extra.point: The build fee usually buys the build only. Tool, hosting and model-usage bills sit on the client's own accounts and are excluded - TwoCore puts them at $20-$150 a month at cost, AutomateNexus at $30-$150/mo, and SuperDupr works an example of an AI receptionist at 400 calls of 3 minutes each coming to about $114 a month across voice platform, model and phone line.

[Inference] Running costs after launch are a common surprise, but no buyer said so in the sources fetched - the evidence is vendors pre-empting it. SuperDupr tells buyers to ask any builder for the monthly running-cost number 'before you sign, not after the first invoice', and both TwoCore and AutomateNexus publish running-cost estimates unprompted. Reason: a vendor writing that warning implies buyers arrive without the number, but this is inference from vendor copy, not a documented buyer complaint.

Paid discovery is commonly credited against the build: Automaly's assessment (from $6,500) is credited in full, NJ AI Automation credits its $500 audit, OVAMIND takes $500 off the sprint, and Agentomte credits its $1,900 audit if the client proceeds. Not every agency sells one - AI Strike Force publishes a written scope after a free call instead.

Post-launch fix windows differ sharply and are the cheapest thing to get wrong. TwoCore includes 30 days of post-launch fixes at no extra charge in the $1,500-$5,000 build; HA Technologies bundles 30-day support with its $4,500 build; OVAMIND's $2,500 sprint includes 14 days of post-launch support.
Fix windows scale with the tier at the productised end: Nyza's fix-it window is 14 days on the $99 Spark build, 30 days on $299 Starter, 60 days on $799 Growth and 90 days on $1,999 Pro.

The shortest published post-launch support window in this set is two weeks: MapScale's Automation Setup includes '2 weeks of post-build support', and Agentomte's from-$9,500 AI Workforce Sprint includes 'two weeks of written post-handover support' with a recorded handover walkthrough. Agentomte's pricing page publishes no fix window at all - the two-week figure comes from the sprint's own service page.

A retainer normally buys monitoring plus small changes; without it every tweak becomes a new scope and a new invoice, and nothing is watching for silent failures when an API or CRM field changes ('Automations don't fail loudly').

Voice agents are metered, and the included-minutes figure is not always published where you would expect it: Dominion publishes 500 included minutes then 25 cents a minute only on its $297/month single-service voice agent, while the $597/$1,097/$1,997 packages list a voice agent with no minutes figure. LuMay's $249/$499/$999 plans include 500/1,000/2,000 minutes at $0.23/$0.22/$0.21 per overage minute.

Setup, training and support are sometimes bundled at the low end - Dominion states all three are included in every package and adds no setup fee - but the same page declines to publish contract, trial, refund or cancellation terms, and lists what it will not promise: a setup time, a number of calls/leads/bookings, texting until carrier approval, or a connection to existing booking/practice software before it is confirmed.

Annual billing is where the discount lives at the productised end: LuMay says annual billing saves the equivalent of two months versus monthly, and its cloud and on-prem tiers are annual subscriptions.

Ownership and exit terms are a real differentiator worth pricing: TwoCore lets the client cancel the retainer with 30 days notice and keep what was built; Agentomte hands over repos, data and keys with no lock-in; Nyza transfers code and assets on delivery; AutomateNexus sells ownership as the headline ('Not a subscription, not per-seat').

buyer_complaints.complaint: Skepticism that 'AI automation agency' offers are mostly template resells - an n8n community thread questions whether buyers get custom work or a generic package.
Fragility and monitoring gaps: an agency owner's public post-mortem describes losing a $2,500/month client after a lead-capture automation ran broken for three days and roughly 40 leads were missed.

Price opacity and incomparability - stated by a vendor, not a buyer: AI Strike Force argues most agencies quote only after a call, and that two agencies can quote the same job ten times apart because they priced different jobs, so quotes must be forced onto the same scope.

price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: Nyza Solutions: $99 / $299 / $799 / $1,999 one-time builds with $49 / $99 / $199 per month care plans, month-to-month. Dominion AI Agency: $297/month single AI voice agent with 500 minutes included then 25 cents a minute; packages at $597 / $1,097 / $1,997 per month with no published minutes figure. Upwork automation freelancers: $35/hr worldwide median, with the US middle half advertising $60-$120/hr and a US median of $80/hr (Upwork Insights by Upsight, Nov 12 2026).
price_ranges.mid_market: One workflow, one-time: TwoCore $1,500-$5,000 per workflow; NJ AI Automation $1,500-$5,000 implementation; AI Strike Force from $2,500 per agent or automation; HA Technologies $4,500 AI Agent Build. Third-party category medians of one-time entry price (AgenticIndex 2026, n=290 directory): $800 for n8n & Make workflow automation (n=32), $1,500 for voice AI (n=35), $4,500 for enterprise RAG (n=28), $5,000 for custom AI agents (n=27); all-agency median entry $2,000 (n=140). Retainers: $250-$2,500/mo (NJ AI Automation $250-$1,000; TwoCore $500-$1,500; Automaly from $2,500; SuperDupr states $200-$2,000 a month for support and monitoring).
price_ranges.full_service_or_custom: LuMay: discovery sprint $10K-$15K, production pilot $25K-$75K, engineering pod $35K-$75K/month, on-prem from $90K/yr + $75K setup. SuperDupr: single agent $5,000-$15,000, workflow automation $10,000-$25,000, multi-agent $25,000-$50,000+. Automaly build from $13,000; Agentomte AI Workforce Sprint from $9,500; OVAMIND retainer $10,000/mo; HA Technologies AI Transformation Partner $8,900/month; AutomateNexus build from $7,500. Hourly for senior build work: The Automators USD $125/hour; OVAMIND $250/hr during launch (normally $500/hr per page); XRAY $250 an hour in blocks of 4, 10 or 20 hours, reported in AI Strike Force's third-party table checked 23 October 2026. Retainer-only agencies in AgenticIndex's 2026 index list a median $5,000/mo (n=30, range $2,000-$15,000).
price_ranges.inference_note: These bands are my grouping of individually cited published prices - not averages calculated from invoices, and no vendor price was estimated. The low band collects complete offers a small business can buy without a sales call: Nyza's $99-$1,999 builds with $49-$199/mo care and Dominion's $297/mo single voice agent, plus the marketplace floor from Upwork Insights ($35/hr worldwide median). The mid band is the cluster of published single-workflow builds and small-business retainers ($1,500-$5,000 one-time; $250-$2,500/mo), and the AgenticIndex category medians are quoted as third-party published-entry statistics, not as vendor list prices. The high band is published multi-agent, pilot and pod prices plus the $5,000/mo median of 30 retainer-only agencies. Where a vendor publishes only a range, the range is reproduced as published; no midpoint is a quote. One earlier figure was withdrawn in this revision: a $97-$250/hr band had been attributed to the Upwork Insights page, which does not show it and contradicts it for offshore work (worldwide median $35/hr); that page is now used only for the rates it actually publishes, and the $125-$250/hr hourly points come from The Automators, OVAMIND and the third-party XRAY row.

implications_for_consultancy: [Inference] The contested, price-anchored tier for a 5-200 staff Middlesex County client is the one-workflow build at $1,500-$5,000 plus $250-$1,500/mo. Reasoning: the two closest comparables publish exactly that (NJ AI Automation: $1,500-$5,000 implementation, $250-$1,000/mo support; TwoCore: $1,500-$5,000 per workflow, $500-$1,500/mo), AI Strike Force enters at $2,500 per agent, and AgenticIndex's third-party category medians for one-time entry sit at $800 (n8n/Make) to $1,500 (voice). A consultancy priced above $5,000 for a first workflow has to justify it with integration depth, not with 'AI'.

[Inference] Buyers in this segment already accept a paid, credited audit at $497-$1,900, with $6,500 the top of the published range. Reasoning: MapScale states $497 (in comparison prose), NJ AI Automation $500 and credits it, OVAMIND $500 for a 90-minute strategy call, HA Technologies $1,200, Agentomte $1,900 and credits it, Automaly from $6,500 and credits it in full. Note the counter-model: AI Strike Force publishes no paid audit at all and argues that for one workflow a written scope after a free call is enough - so a paid assessment has to be positioned as a deliverable, not a toll gate.

[Inference] The weakest-defended price point is the $297-$600/mo 'AI receptionist/automation' package. Reasoning: Dominion sells $597/mo with setup, training and support included, and Nyza sells $99-$799 builds with $49-$199/mo care. Competing there as a local consultant means competing with a productised build and a published price; better to position the monthly retainer at $750-$2,500 with named hours, monitoring and a quarterly review, where NJ AI Automation ($250-$1,000), TwoCore ($500-$1,500) and Automaly (from $2,500) leave room, and AgenticIndex's fractional-advisory retainer median of $3,500/mo (third-party, n=13) marks the ceiling.

[Inference] A higher price is defensible when the deliverable is integration and continuity, not the agent. Reasoning: every vendor that publishes exclusions points at the same gaps - tool/API costs on the client's accounts ($20-$150/mo at TwoCore and $30-$150/mo at AutomateNexus), Dominion refusing to promise call volumes or a connection to practice software 'before we have confirmed it works', and TwoCore's point that automations fail silently when an API changes. A local firm that owns those gaps (accounts in the client's name, monitored response times, documented handover) is selling what the cheap tier explicitly excludes.

[Inference] Hourly work is a weak headline but a useful change-order rate. Reasoning: US automation freelancers advertise a median $80/hr with a $60-$120 middle half (Upwork Insights), NJ-serving The Automators publishes USD $125/hour, OVAMIND lists $250/hr during its launch period against a stated normal $500/hr, and the third-party table puts XRAY at $250 an hour in 4/10/20-hour blocks. A local rate of $125-$175/hr sits inside that spread; quoting a fixed price first matches how nearly all published US offers in this set are structured.

[Inference] Retainers above roughly $2,500/mo put the firm in a different buying conversation. Reasoning: AgenticIndex's retainer-only cohort (30 agencies) medians $5,000/mo (third-party), and the fractional/embedded offers (LuMay pod $35K-$75K/month, OVAMIND $10,000/mo, HA Technologies $8,900/month, Agentomte $2,900/mo) are sold as embedded capacity. For a 5-200 staff NJ business, that is a budget-holder decision; the $750-$2,500 band is an owner or office-manager decision and closes faster.

[Inference] Expect price comparison against Upwork, and price the difference explicitly. Reasoning: US automation freelancers advertise a median $80/hr and the worldwide median is $35/hr, so a client can always find a cheaper build. The defensible line is the published-vendor pattern of 30-day fix windows, accounts in the client's name, monitoring and cancellation-with-handover - deliverables a marketplace freelancer rarely documents.

[Inference] A take-it-or-leave-it public price list is itself a differentiator in this segment. Reasoning: AgenticIndex found 85 of 290 agencies (29%) publish no price at all and 205 (71%) do, with 113 of those 205 sitting in a $1k-$5k minimum-budget tier. Publishing a pilot price, a build band and a retainer band - as TwoCore, Agentomte, NJ AI Automation and Nyza do - removes the discovery-call gate that the publishing vendors themselves complain about.
caveats: All prices were read on 2026-11-12 from the linked pages unless the page itself states an earlier date (SuperDupr 'as of October 2026'; Agentomte 'current as of July 2026'; AI Strike Force's 14-agency table 'checked on 23 October 2026').
Many of the vendors that publish clean prices are small or solo operations. Their published prices are real list prices, but they are not evidence of what a 50-person New Jersey company negotiates.

Two agency comparison sources used here (AI Strike Force's 14-agency table and AgenticIndex's 290-agency report) are compiled by parties with a commercial interest in the category, and AI Strike Force appears in its own table. Figures they attribute to other agencies were not all re-opened at source by me; the XRAY $250/hr row is one such third-party figure and is labelled as third-party wherever it is used.

MapScale's $497 audit price appears only in the page's price-comparison prose, not as a line-item price against the Systems Audit service, and MapScale publishes no price for Automation Setup or Done For You. Its $8,000-$25,000 / $4,000-$10,000 / $1,000-$3,500 monthly comparison tiers are the vendor's citation of third-party pricing guides and are not used as MapScale prices here.

Agentomte publishes no post-launch fix window on its pricing page; the two-week post-handover written support cited here comes from its AI Workforce Sprint service page. An earlier version of this brief attributed 30 days to Agentomte, which was wrong.

Reddit, Indie Hackers and Clutch blocked direct retrieval (HTTP 403 or JavaScript-only). The Reddit and Indie Hackers items come from thread titles as returned in search results, and the Clutch hourly rate and minimum project size come from listing metadata in search snippets; all should be treated as directional. A Clutch 'most common project size' figure carried in an earlier version could not be confirmed and was removed.

Vendor case studies (Streamline IQ) and third-party write-ups (Wealthy Tent) report seller-side prices and buyer outcomes supplied by the seller; no invoice, contract or buyer confirmation was seen. The Wealthy Tent page's own headline total ($23,000) does not match its four published prices ($23,650).
Published entry prices are often the smallest possible scope. Where a vendor publishes a band ('$1,500-$5,000'), the band is reproduced as published and no midpoint should be treated as a quote.
data_gaps: No New Jersey or Middlesex County agency published a full rate card with tiers, overage and cancellation terms; the closest local data are NJ AI Automation (audit/build/support only) and The Automators (Calgary-based, markets to NJ, USD $125/hour).

No independent survey of what small US businesses actually pay AI automation agencies was found. The AgenticIndex and Upwork Insights datasets are analyses of published and advertised prices, not invoices, and AgenticIndex's own methodology note says its directory is curated rather than a random sample.
Cancellation and refund terms are unstated by most vendors, including Dominion (explicitly), MapScale, AutomateNexus, SuperDupr and AI Strike Force.

No public hourly rate was found for an NJ/NYC agency serving Middlesex County from its own page; the hourly data points are The Automators (USD $125/hour), OVAMIND ($250/hr launch), XRAY ($250/hr, third-party table only) and the Upwork marketplace index.

Free trials were not found at any agency in this set; the closest equivalents are conditional refunds (Agentomte audit refund, Automaly assessment refund) and free 20-30 minute consultations (MapScale, SuperDupr, AI Strike Force, The Automators, AutomateNexus).

Buyer-side complaint evidence is thin: review platforms (Clutch, Trustpilot, Capterra) and forums (Reddit, Indie Hackers) blocked retrieval, so the three complaints listed are directional and two rest on thread titles only. No first-person buyer account of a monthly invoice from this category was located.

Included voice-minute allowances are published only on single-service or entry tiers (Dominion $297 service; LuMay voice plans); the mid-tier package allowances at Dominion remain unpublished and could not be established from any page.
